The canonical `templates/prepare-merge-driver.ts` runs `pm merge install` on every npm `prepare`. npm 10 also runs `prepare` during `npm pack`, even with `--ignore-scripts`. Packing a package therefore has a side effect on the packing repository's `.git/config`. Packing is supposed to be read-only, and parallel pack calls in test suites race on the config lock.

Observed in [pm-todos run 37647796743](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-todos/actions/runs/37647796743/job/112882996197) on Node 22: a packed-fixture test failed with `Cannot install repository-local merge drivers … no other Git process holds its lock`. Upstream lock handling is tracked in unbraind/pm-cli#1424.

Suggestion: in the template, skip the install (with one notice) when `process.env.npm_command === "pack"` or `"publish"`, which npm sets for lifecycle scripts. Clone-time `npm install` / `npm ci` keep registering the drivers. Then re-copy the template across the fleet through the usual pm-ops rollout.
